title: End-to-End Training of Multi-Document Reader and Retriever for Open-Domain Question Answering
layout_note: A wide single-panel graph whose two training objectives sit as two boxes on the top edge. The left half is the retrieval chain: Evidence Docs drops to a Stale Evidence Doc Encoder, which elbows right (labelled 'Asynchronous Index Refresh') into the Distributed Evidence Doc Index over GPUs; the question enters from the top centre, goes down through the Question Encoder to f_e(q) and on into the same index via 'top-k MIPS'. The index outputs Top-k Docs, where the graph forks: one branch rises through the Evidence Encoder to Inner Product (which also receives a horizontal line from the Question Encoder) and then runs up and right to Retriever Training; the other turns down-right through a Preprocessor into the reader on the right, which climbs bottom-to-top from x_i, x_j, x_k through the T5 Encoder and a Concat box into two T5 Decoders whose outputs p(a|q,z_i) and p(a|q,Z) rise into Retriever Training and Reader Training.
grouping: No background panels, containers, brackets or legend; the parts are grouped by column position and by two colour families. Light orange marks the retriever's two encoders (Question Encoder, Evidence Encoder) and lime green the reader's T5 modules (T5 Encoder, the right-hand T5 Decoder). The reader occupies the right third as its own bottom-to-top column; the retrieval chain fills the left and centre. The two T5 Decoders are linked by a thin curved arc labelled 'Shared Parameters', and the two Training boxes on the top edge act as the two sinks, each above the output that feeds it.
shapes_depth: Flat, no shadows, thin black outlines, sans-serif regular-weight labels. Corner shape separates kinds of box: every network module (Question Encoder, Evidence Encoder, Stale Evidence Doc Encoder, T5 Encoder, both T5 Decoders) is a square-cornered rectangle, while data, operations and objectives (Evidence Docs, the index, Top-k Docs, Inner Product, Preprocessor, the g_e(x_i)...g_e(x_k) concat box, Retriever Training, Reader Training) are white rounded rectangles. Per-document repetition is drawn as a deck: the T5 Encoder has two faded pale-green copies offset up and right behind it, and the white T5 Decoder has two grey-outlined copies behind it. Arrows are thin lines with filled triangular heads, straight or as orthogonal elbows with rounded bends; the path of the first document x_i is black while the paths of x_j, x_k and their extra decoder outputs are mid-grey. No tensors are drawn; quantities are bold-italic LaTeX math labels placed beside the arrows, and the raw inputs (question q, x_i, x_j, x_k, a) are unboxed.
proposed_highlight: The figure never names the method; the paper's trainable modules are picked out by fill alone (light orange for the two retriever encoders, lime green for the T5 Encoder and reader decoder), with the caption acting as the legend for what colour means. Untinted counterparts sit next to them: the white Stale Evidence Doc Encoder feeding the index, and the white T5 Decoder stack, which is tied to the green decoder by the 'Shared Parameters' arc and has an 'SG' label with double-slash ticks across its three output arrows. The two Training objectives are plain white rounded boxes, not emphasised.
lesson: Fill colour is reserved for modules with trainable parameters (one hue per sub-model, explained in the caption), so a white twin of a coloured module, such as the stale document encoder or the parameter-sharing decoder copy, reads as frozen or borrowed without a lock icon or legend.
notes: Venue and year from the arXiv journal-ref (verified). 'operator-glyph' is the stop-gradient mark: short double-slash ticks drawn across the decoder output arrows, named once by the 'SG' label. 'equation' covers the inline math labels (f_e(q), f_d(z_i), X_Z, p(a|q,z_i), p(a|q,Z)). Arrow labels in plain text: 'top-k MIPS', 'Concat', 'Asynchronous Index Refresh'. The method name EMDR2 appears only in the caption.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: open-domain question answering with an end-to-end trained retriever and multi-document reader

core.what: the retriever chain fills the left and centre (stale doc encoder -> distributed index -> top-k MIPS with the question embedding -> Top-k Docs), and the retrieved documents feed a stacked T5 encoder/decoder column on the right that ends in two 'Training' sinks on the top edge

relations.form: a rounded 'Distributed Evidence Doc Index over GPUs' box sits below the question path; f_e(q) drops into it via 'top-k MIPS' and Top-k Docs (Z) leaves it to the right, all as text boxes

Evidence Docs -> Stale Evidence Doc Encoder -> index runs down the left with an 'Asynchronous Index Refresh' label; Top-k Docs -> Preprocessor -> x_i, x_j, x_k -> T5 Encoder runs along the bottom right
per-document copies of T5 Encoder and T5 Decoder are drawn as fanned stacks of offset boxes, the front copy solid and the others faded, with grey arrows for the extra documents
a curved arc labelled 'Shared Parameters' joins the white T5 Decoder stack (with SG stop-gradient marks on its outputs) and the green T5 Decoder that reads the concatenated encodings
the question embedding and the document embedding f_d(z_i) meet at an 'Inner Product' box whose output rises via an elbow to 'Retriever Training'
the encodings g_e(x_i) ... g_e(x_k) meet in one 'Concat' box whose output X_Z joins the answer a in the green T5 Decoder

channels.colour: trainable module: orange = retriever encoders, green = reader T5 encoder/decoder, white = frozen or stale copies (stale doc encoder, the stop-gradient decoder stack); data, index and objectives are all white text boxes
channels.shape: rounded box = data or store, square-cornered box = encoder or computation; fanned stack = per-document copies
channels.line: black arrows = main data path, grey arrows = the other k-1 documents' paths, a curved arc = shared parameters; '//' marks = stop gradient

quality.strengths: Fill is reserved for trainable modules (orange retriever, green reader) so frozen copies read as white; fanned stacks with faded copies show per-document processing without drawing k boxes; the two objectives sit as sinks along the top edge, keeping retriever and reader training visibly separate.
quality.weaknesses: Documents, index and objectives are all identical white text boxes, so the store and the retrieved items are not drawn as data; objectives are written as typeset likelihoods p(a | q, z_i); the inner-product output takes a long elbow up to Retriever Training, and the Preprocessor branch bends under the docs box, so paths are long and turning.

insights.structure: One unframed graph: the retrieval chain (Evidence Docs, Stale Evidence Doc Encoder, Distributed Evidence Doc Index, Question Encoder) fills the left and centre, the T5 reader forms a bottom-to-top column on the right, and two 'Training' boxes sit on the top edge as sinks.
insights.data: Everything is a white rounded text box with math labels (f_e(q), f_d(z_i), g_e(x_i), X_Z, p(a|q,z_i)); the k retrieved documents are drawn as stacked translucent copies of the T5 Encoder and T5 Decoder with grey arrows for x_j, x_k.
insights.emphasis: Trainable modules are the only filled boxes - light orange for the two retriever encoders, lime green for the T5 Encoder and the reader-side T5 Decoder - while the white stale encoder and white decoder stack (tied by a 'Shared Parameters' arc and an 'SG' stop-gradient mark) read as frozen copies.
insights.flow: Mostly bottom-to-top: the question drops from the top centre to the index, Top-k Docs forks up through the Evidence Encoder to the Inner Product and right through the Preprocessor into the reader column, which rises to p(a|q,Z) and Reader Training.
insights.avoid: The colour code is explained only in the caption and the 'SG' double-slash notation is undefined in the figure; the long horizontal line from the Question Encoder to the Inner Product cuts across the middle.

arrangement.units: no enclosures; retriever chain on the left/centre and reader column on the right, grouped by position and two fill colours
arrangement.inputs_as: plain text boxes 'question (q)' at top centre and 'Evidence Docs (D)' at the left edge, plus answer a entering the right decoder from below
arrangement.shared: curved 'Shared Parameters' arc between the two T5 Decoders; the Distributed Evidence Doc Index is shared by question and document paths
